title: Ancient Trees in Bulgaria: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Bulgaria's oldest tree is down to one living branch, dated to about 345 AD by an actual ring count. Three cities mapped, six trees.
intro: Bulgaria's oldest tree is not its most impressive one to look at anymore. A 1982 core sample counted 1,637 rings in the Granit Oak, dating its germination to around 345 and giving Bulgaria a tree age nobody has to guess at, but a 1969 storm and falling groundwater have since reduced it to a single living branch. Higher up, in Pirin National Park above Bansko, Baikushev's Pine carries a gentler kind of age claim: tradition holds it was already standing when Khan Asparuh founded the First Bulgarian Empire around 681, a repeated figure of about 1,300 years rather than a measured one. Sofia supplies the political history in between, a mulberry linked to national hero Vasil Levski, an oak named for the poet Pencho Slaveykov, a spruce planted for Ivan Vazov. Three cities mapped so far, six trees, from a dying record-holder to a living tradition.
